([[Richmond, Indiana]]) | college = [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU]] (2016–2020) | highlights = * First-team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] (2020) * Second-team All-Big 12 (2019) | medal_templates = }} '''Desmond Michael Bane''' (born June 25, 1998) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU Horned Frogs]]. ==Early life== After he was born, Bane, his mother, Marissa, and his sister often moved around, living with relatives because his mother was young and not prepared for the demands of parenting. When he was two years old, he started living with his great-grandparents, who raised him in [[Richmond, Indiana]] for the rest of his childhood.{{cite web |last1=Jiménez |first1=Jesús |title=Great-grandparents molded Seton Catholic star |url=https://www.pal-item.com/story/sports/high-school/2016/03/26/great-grandparents-molded-seton-catholic-star/81989968/ |website=[[Palladium-Item]] |accessdate=December 4, 2019 |date=March 26, 2016}} At age 13, Bane discovered that his father, Etieno Ekiko, lived in [[Nigeria]]. Growing up, he found more success in [[baseball]] than in basketball but preferred the latter sport.{{cite web |last1=Davison |first1=Drew |title=Overlooked? Counted out? Desmond Bane knows what TCU is facing all too well |url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/college/big-12/texas-christian-university/article227469919.html |website=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]] |accessdate=December 4, 2019 |date=March 13, 2019}} Bane focused on baseball until eighth grade, with his great-grandfather coaching at the youth level, and also played [[American football|football]] and [[association football|soccer]]. ==High school career== Bane played basketball for [[Seton Catholic High School (Richmond, Indiana)|Seton Catholic High School]], a small [[private school]] in Richmond, Indiana. He was drawn to the school because it appointed Josh Jurgens, who coached him in third grade, as head basketball coach during his eighth-grade season. As a senior, Bane averaged a state-high 30 points, 11.5 rebounds, 6.1 assists and 3.2 blocks per game. He scored a school-record 62 points and nine three-pointers in a win over [[Lincoln Senior High School (Cambridge City, Indiana)|Lincoln Senior High School]].{{cite web |last1=Jiménez |first1=Jesús |title=8 unforgettable Desmond Bane moments |url=https://www.pal-item.com/story/sports/college/2018/03/13/8-unforgettable-desmond-bane-moments/421417002/ |website=[[Palladium-Item]] |accessdate=December 4, 2019 |date=March 13, 2018}} He was named MVP of the Wettig Memorial Holiday Tournament. Bane scored 1,991 points over his four-year career, surpassing 1988 [[Indiana Mr. Basketball]] winner Woody Austin for the most in [[Wayne County, Indiana|Wayne County]] history. He did not receive an [[NCAA Division I]] offer until his senior season, when [[Furman Paladins men's basketball|Furman]] offered him at the end of November early signing period. On May 12, 2016, Bane committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU]].{{cite web |last1=Jiménez |first1=Jesús |title=How TCU and Desmond Bane became a perfect match |url=https://www.pal-item.com/story/sports/college/2018/03/17/march-madness-2018-how-tcu-and-desmond-bane-became-perfect-match/434658002/ |website=[[Palladium-Item]] |accessdate=December 5, 2019 |date=March 17, 2018}} He was not rated by major recruiting services [[247Sports.com|247Sports]], [[ESPN]], or [[Rivals.com|Rivals]]. ==College career== [[File:Desmond Bane 3.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Bane with [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU]] in 2020]] Bane earned [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] Newcomer of the Week honors after scoring 18 points and pulling down seven rebounds against [[Bradley Braves men's basketball|Bradley]]. He had 16 points including three free throws with two seconds remaining to help TCU defeat first-ranked [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], 85–82, in the quarterfinals of the Phillips 66 Big 12 Championship. Bane helped TCU win the NIT as a freshman, contributing nine points in the title game against [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]]. He averaged 7.1 points and 2.9 rebounds per game and making 13 starts. In an 89–83 victory over [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]], Bane scored a season-high 27 points. As a sophomore, Bane averaged 12.5 points and 4.1 rebounds per game and his 47.2% 3-point percentage led the Big 12. In the NCAA Tournament, Bane had five points, four rebounds, four assists, a steal, and a block in the first-round loss to [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]]. As a junior, Bane was named to the Second Team All-Big 12.{{cite news |last1=Lopez |first1=Selby |title=Baylor stars earn multiple All-Big 12 honors. See the full list of conference award winners |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/2019/03/10/baylor-stars-earn-multiple-all-big-12-honors-see-the-full-list-of-conference-award-winners/ |accessdate=December 6, 2019 |work=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |date=March 10, 2019}} He had a career-high 34 points in the team's regular-season finale against [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] and scored 30 points versus [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]] in the second round of the NIT. Bane averaged 15.2 points per game to lead the team, 5.7 rebounds per game and shot 42.5% from behind the arc. After the season, he "tested the waters" of the NBA draft but returned to TCU.{{cite news |last1=Straka |first1=Dean |title=TCU leading-scorer Desmond Bane to enter name in draft, test NBA waters |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/2019/04/10/tcu-leading-scorer-desmond-bane-to-enter-name-in-draft-test-nba-waters/ |accessdate=December 6, 2019 |work=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |date=April 10, 2019}} As a senior, Bane was named to the First Team All-Big 12. {{cite press release|url=https://big12sports.com/news/2020/3/7/mens-basketball-all-big-12-awards-announced.aspx|title=Men’s Basketball All-Big 12 Awards Announced|work=[[Big 12 Conference]]|date=March 8, 2020 |accessdate=March 8, 2020}} Bane averaged 16.6 points and 6.3 rebounds per game, and his 44.2% three-point percentage led the Big 12. On March 2, 2020, Bane was named Big 12 player of the week after scoring 23 points in a 75–72 upset over second-ranked [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]].{{cite web|url=https://big12sports.com/news/2020/3/2/tcu-texas-collect-mens-basketball-weekly-awards.aspx|title=TCU, Texas Collect Men’s Basketball Weekly Awards|publisher=Big 12 Conference|date=March 2,
